about: Held-out pairs for the past-value guard of the rung 2.5 admission rule, registered before any run: no model has been asked any of these rows. The 2026-10-12 replay found the proposed gate retiring an older claim that records only a past value ('lived in Utrecht until 2025', a dated re-anchor restatement), which the contradiction probe had kept. These rows test the amended past-value rule in both directions, worded apart from gate_pairs.json, gate_pairs_heldout.json and the prompt's examples, in other places and domains: 'past-ended' rows (an older claim with a stated end, in the past tense, or in a restatement's 'As of <date>, when ...' shape) must not be retired; 'present-dated' rows (an older present-tense claim carrying a date, as claude-sonnet-5-5's extractor writes them) must still be. Class 'past-then-past' is the rot benchmark's history pair. Class 'case' holds the trip case's own restatement shape, reported apart. Bars, from the acceptance plan (item 3b): on each model, proposed gate with the amended prompt, every 'present-dated' row retired in at least two of three samples, and no retirement in any 'past-ended' or 'past-then-past' sample.
